symptom: `exec` of `create or modify microflow` cost about 20 ms per statement on a project of 5,373 units, and grew with the project (mendixlabs/mxcli#1842, ako/mxcli#2160).
cause: refuseNameClash runs before every create. For each kind in the name space it called loadNameSet, which builds the qualified name of every element of that kind in the project and a lower-cased copy of each -- 5,000 names and their garbage per statement -- to look up one name.
fix: For microflows, nanoflows and pages, build the set from the elements whose own name folds to the target's (strings.EqualFold, a superset of the set's ToLower match). 200 updates: 4.37 s -> 3.45 s, written files byte-identical.
insight: The item on the list was 'reconcile parses a document seven times'. The profile said reconcile was 0.2 s of 4.0 s and this check 0.66 s plus its share of a 39% GC. Two items in a row on that list were wrong about where the time was; profile the statement before picking the function. Module scoping (as done for entities) would not have helped the benchmark, whose filler flows share one module -- filtering on the short name does not depend on how the project is laid out.
test: mdl/executor/named_name_set_pedapp_test.go: every lookup answered as the full set answers it, for stored, upper, lower, other-module and absent names of each kind, plus the System microflows; fails if the lookups are one-sided or the set is not filtered. Three mutations each fail.
